questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: An english speaking university with more English courses available. The right courses (for me it was psychology courses relevant for a sociology student). And a beautiful area, with much to explore beyond university.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Mostly very easy. The few times I was in doubt, it was easy to get in touch with someone who could and would help.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Before arrival there was an online presentation for exchange students, which provided most of the help. I personally did not receive assistance, but only because I declined - there were many opportunities for assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very difficult. Vancouver is known for its housing problems, so whatever options are available, are generally very expensive. I managed to find a good place in the end, that I could afford because of the shared income of my husband and myself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Apply early to lists through UBC, so you can avoid applying through sites. And when you do apply, be very careful with scams. 

But, I found that it was worth it. Vancouver is a beautiful place, and offers more than just its city centre and the campus. Also, public transport to UBC is excellent, so it's easy enough to live off campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I don't remember too much of it - maybe because they made it very easy. There was a lot of information long before arrival, so the only thing to do when I landed was to pick up my student ID

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, I sadly don't remember too much of it. But of what I do remember, any help that wasn't immediately available, was easy to find elsewhere.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Almost completely. One course was full, but they quickly helped me register for another, and made sure to fit me in.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Simply follow the guidelines you are sent. Everything is far less complicated that it might appear. Also, it's easy enough to change classes if you are unhappy with the original ones after the first few weeks

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can only speak for the psychology department.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All 3rd year courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In many ways the same: lectures and reading with focus on critical discussions and in-depth understanding of the material. However, there is less group work seeing as exams at UBC are mostly individual multiple choice exams, and for the same reason, classes tend to lead up to the next midterm, so it feels like you are doing several sub-semesters.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Social psychology
Evolutionary psychology
Personality Psychology
Cultural psychology
Behavioral cognition

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them, no doubt. Each one had an incredible professor with so much knowledge and passion and a will to teach. But I think that the two courses that gave me most "fresh perspective" from my courses in UCPH, was evolutionary and cultural psychology. In each their way they tought "hard" topics with very "soft" measures and open perspectives.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: My husband forgot to get insured, so a simple trip to the doctor cost us 8000kr. And housing was (as described earlier).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: As described before, housing is very expensive. The same goes for short term housing like hotels, hostels and the like. Books cost me nothing because the we're either offered as free PDF's, or easy to find for free.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't enroll in any myself, but heard many great things about them from both exchange and home students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I did not apply to any myself, so I am not sure. But they have a big event on the first day with open stands hosted by students where you can sign up or simply inquire.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: As I didn't do any, I can't say. But if hiking and visiting greater British Columbia counts, I absolutely recommend that!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See British Columbia! Be it big adventures a weekend in Squamish, or simply a day to Horseshoe Bay, the nature is simply stunning and more than worth your attention and time. Vancouver city also has heaps to offer, from markets to cafees, museums, parks, and of course the great (and plentiful) Asian cuisine.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Vancouver is very multicultural already.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be kind and respectful as always, and understand that students come from all over the world, and therefore have different social behaviors.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None that were significant or challenging. Be aware of tipping culture?

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity. Vancouver is not like the rest of Canada - it is a pot of Canadians, Americans, Chinese, Korean, Japanese and so much more.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
You are not visiting a Canadian university - you are visiting a multicultural university!

The exams are multiple choice midterms, so manage your time well to not drown in exams! It's not like doing 1 every end-of-term like we are used to.

Don't worry about the beucracy. There is plenty of help to find both online and in person!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be ready for a different kind of exams and different grading policy. Multiple choice midterms are easy enough, but count towards your final grades, and it can be very challenging if you are not prepared for it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Either my courses (I have been so inspired by my professors!) or visiting the nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exams. If you're not keeping up, it is easy to have a lot of pressure around the midterms - and there ARE a lot of them.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
